hypothesis: Large language models (LLMs) can enhance drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction by leveraging their ability to process and synthesize complex biological data, thereby improving the accuracy of binding affinity predictions through advanced representation learning techniques. This hypothesis is supported by the successful application of deep learning architectures in DTI prediction, which have shown that models utilizing sequence information can outperform traditional methods in predicting binding affinities, indicating that LLMs could similarly benefit from such approaches in drug discovery contexts [46:1][46:14].
